tiers.name: EU / EEA / Switzerland
tiers.summary: No visa and no residence permit. Enrol, arrange health insurance, and register the address within two weeks of arrival.

tiers.name: Visa-free entry, permit obtained inside Germany
tiers.summary: No visa needed to enter. The student travels first, then applies for the residence permit inside Germany within 90 days. This skips the embassy appointment entirely.

tiers.name: National (Type D) student visa
tiers.summary: A full Type D student visa before travel. The variable that matters most is appointment availability at the student's local German mission.

notes.cbse: APS applies: the certificate is issued by an Indian board. From WS 2026/27 the anabin criteria also require 70% of the maximum achievable marks in Class XII before any German university will assess the file.
notes.isc: APS applies: the certificate is issued by an Indian board. The 70% Class XII floor from WS 2026/27 applies here too.
notes.state: APS applies, and state boards are the most likely to need an individual anabin check. The 70% Class XII floor applies.
notes.ib: No APS. The IB Diploma is not issued by an Indian institution, so an Indian passport holder with an IB Diploma falls outside APS India's remit. The 70% Class XII floor does not apply either.
notes.alevel: No APS. Cambridge A Levels are not issued by an Indian institution. Direct entry normally needs three A Levels; check anabin for the specific combination.
notes.us: No APS. A US high school diploma alone rarely gives direct entry - it usually needs AP subjects or a year of university, otherwise the student is on a Studienkolleg year.

options.name: India
options.note: APS India, New Delhi. The visa file goes through the Consular Services Portal first; the VFS appointment link only appears at the end of a completed application. Remonstration has been abolished in India since 1 January 2024, so the first submission is the only one.

options.name: UAE
options.note: The German missions in Abu Dhabi and Dubai, through the UAE VFS centres. A student on a CBSE or ISC certificate still falls under APS India even though the school is in the UAE, because the board is Indian - confirm with APS India before assuming either way.

tiers.name: EU / EEA / Switzerland
tiers.summary: Free movement. No MVV, no residence permit, no TB test. Register with the municipality after arrival.

tiers.name: MVV-exempt
tiers.summary: No entry visa needed, but the student still needs a VVR residence permit. The university applies for it; the student collects it in the Netherlands rather than at a consulate.
tiers.exact_quote: Your nationality determines whether you need an MVV. You do not need an MVV if you have the nationality of one of these countries.

tiers.name: MVV required
tiers.summary: The university runs the TEV procedure - entry visa and residence permit applied for together. The student collects the MVV sticker at a Dutch mission before travelling.
tiers.exact_quote: Your nationality determines whether you need an MVV.

notes.cbse: Standard XII is weighed against HAVO/VWO. Several universities accept only CBSE and CISCE and will not look at a state board, and many require a first year of Indian university on top.
notes.isc: Treated alongside CBSE by the universities that publish a country rule; the same HAVO/VWO comparison applies.
notes.state: The weakest position. Check each university's country page - a number of them accept only CBSE and CISCE.
notes.ib: Direct entry at every Dutch research university. No foundation year, no first-year-of-university condition.
notes.alevel: Direct entry, normally on three A Levels. Subject requirements are programme-specific.
notes.us: A diploma alone is usually not enough for a research university - AP subjects or a year of college is the normal condition.

options.name: India
options.note: Documents need an apostille from the Ministry of External Affairs. The MVV sticker is collected at New Delhi, Mumbai or Bengaluru within a three-month window.

options.name: UAE
options.note: Documents are attested through the UAE Ministry of Foreign Affairs rather than the Indian MEA chain. The MVV is collected at the Dutch mission in Abu Dhabi or Dubai.

tiers.name: EU / EEA / Switzerland
tiers.summary: No visa and no residence permit. Enrol and arrange health cover; nothing in the visa chain applies.

tiers.name: Non-EU
tiers.summary: A VLS-TS long-stay student visa, validated online within three months of arrival. Whether the file runs through Etudes en France depends on where the student lives, not on the passport.

notes.cbse: There is no French APS or anabin. Class XII is assessed by the institution itself, so the bar differs school by school.
notes.isc: Assessed by the institution; no central recognition step.
notes.state: Assessed by the institution; expect more scrutiny than CBSE or ISC.
notes.ib: Widely recognised for direct entry, including at the grandes ecoles.
notes.alevel: Recognised for direct entry; subject combination matters more than the grades at most institutions.
notes.us: Usually needs AP subjects or SAT alongside the diploma.

options.name: A country covered by Etudes en France
options.note: The Etudes en France procedure is compulsory and it is keyed on where the student lives, not the passport. It applies even at the private grandes ecoles: the school can admit the student directly, but without an EEF file there is no visa. 73 countries are covered, India and the UAE among them.
options.exact_quote: Students who reside in one of the countries affected by this procedure must make a specific request for enrolment.

options.name: India (Etudes en France)
options.note: Campus France India. The EEF fee rose from INR 18,500 to INR 20,000, and the academic interview is held in India.

options.name: UAE (Etudes en France)
options.note: Campus France UAE, not Campus France India - the procedure follows residence. An Indian passport holder living in Dubai files through the UAE office and pays the UAE fee, and the interview is held there.

options.name: A country not covered
options.note: No Etudes en France file. The student applies to the institution directly and then to the French consulate for the VLS-TS.

tiers.name: EU / EEA / Switzerland
tiers.summary: No visa, no pre-enrolment quota, no Universitaly step. Apply to the university directly and enrol.

tiers.name: Non-EU residing abroad
tiers.summary: Universitaly pre-enrolment is mandatory and the student competes inside the reserved non-EU quota for the programme. Type D study visa before travel, then a permesso di soggiorno within 8 working days of landing.

notes.cbse: Class XII clears the 12-years-of-schooling bar on its own. Recognition runs either through a CIMEA statement or a consular Declaration of Value.
notes.isc: Same as CBSE - 12 years of schooling is satisfied, then CIMEA or a Declaration of Value.
notes.state: 12 years is satisfied, but expect the consulate to scrutinise a state board record more closely.
notes.ib: The IB Diploma is recognised directly and CIMEA processes it quickly; no Declaration of Value is normally needed.
notes.alevel: Recognised, but Italy counts years of schooling - a student with fewer than 12 years may need a supplementary year or university credits.
notes.us: A US diploma is 12 years and is accepted, though some universities ask for AP subjects.

options.name: India
options.note: The Indian attestation chain applies: HRD attestation first, then MEA apostille, before the Declaration of Value at the competent Italian consulate.

options.name: UAE
options.note: Attestation runs through the UAE Ministry of Foreign Affairs, and the Declaration of Value is issued by the Italian consulate in Dubai or the embassy in Abu Dhabi - not by the Indian posts.

tiers.name: EU / EEA / Switzerland
tiers.summary: No student visa. The academic route (homologacion or UNEDasiss) still applies, because that is keyed on the qualification, not the passport.

tiers.name: Non-EU
tiers.summary: A student visa before travel, then a TIE card after arrival. The academic route runs in parallel and is the longer of the two.

notes.cbse: Homologacion of Class XII is the single biggest scheduling risk in the whole Spanish chain - it gates the public-university route and routinely takes months.
notes.isc: Same homologacion route and the same waiting time as CBSE.
notes.state: Same route; sworn translation of a state board record takes longer to arrange.
notes.ib: UNEDasiss accepts the IB Diploma directly and homologacion is generally not required for the public route - this removes the longest wait in the chain.
notes.alevel: UNEDasiss handles A Levels through its own accreditation route; check which PCE subjects the target degree needs.
notes.us: Handled through UNEDasiss; a US diploma normally needs PCE subject exams to compete for a public place.

options.name: India
options.note: Apostille and sworn translation of the school record, and a Police Clearance Certificate from the Regional Passport Office. There is no PCE exam centre in India, which is its own scheduling problem.

options.name: UAE
options.note: UAE MOFA attestation rather than the Indian apostille chain, and the police certificate comes from the UAE authorities. Confirm the nearest PCE exam centre before booking anything.

tiers.name: EU / EFTA
tiers.summary: Free movement under the AFMP. Enter without a visa, then register with the commune within 14 days and apply for a B permit for study.

tiers.name: Third-country national
tiers.summary: A national D visa applied for in person at the Swiss representation in the country of residence, then registration with the commune within 14 days and a cantonal B permit.

notes.cbse: The swissuniversities country table is the gate, and for India it is restrictive - Class XII alone is generally not admissible for direct entry at HSG. Read the table before anything else.
notes.isc: Same swissuniversities country table and the same restriction as CBSE.
notes.state: Same table; a state board record is the least likely to clear direct entry.
notes.ib: Admissible for direct entry - this is the realistic route into Swiss universities for a student in an international school.
notes.alevel: Admissible for direct entry, subject to the subject combination the university requires.
notes.us: A diploma alone is normally not admissible; APs or a year of university are usually required.

options.name: India
options.note: The D visa is lodged in person at the Swiss Embassy in New Delhi. Its checklist makes IELTS or TOEFL mandatory even where the university itself does not ask for one - HSG says no language proof is needed and the embassy checklist disagrees.

options.name: UAE
options.note: The D visa is lodged at the Swiss Embassy in Abu Dhabi. Check its own document checklist - the New Delhi language-proof rule is a New Delhi rule, not a Swiss-wide one.

tiers.name: Student's Pass only
tiers.summary: A Student's Pass through SOLAR and ICA. No separate entry visa - the IPA letter is enough to travel.
tiers.exact_quote: Nationals of the listed countries require a visa to enter Singapore.

tiers.name: Student's Pass and an entry visa
tiers.summary: A Student's Pass plus an entry visa. The IPA letter doubles as the single-journey entry visa, and ICA takes about two weeks rather than one because of it.
tiers.exact_quote: Nationals of the listed countries require a visa to enter Singapore.

notes.cbse: Direct entry - Class XII needs no equivalence and no foundation year. NUS and NTU publish completely different thresholds, so read each one rather than a single 'Indian cutoff'.
notes.isc: Direct entry on the same basis as CBSE.
notes.state: Direct entry, though the published indicative grade profiles are built on CBSE and ISC records.
notes.ib: Direct entry. NUS does not publish IB grade profiles at all, so there is no cutoff to quote - only the subject prerequisites.
notes.alevel: Direct entry. The published indicative grade profiles for Singapore-Cambridge A Levels are the clearest numbers either university releases.
notes.us: Accepted with SAT or AP alongside the diploma.

options.name: India
options.note: Nothing India-specific in the application itself. The entry visa follows the passport, not the address - an Indian passport needs one wherever the student lives.

options.name: UAE
options.note: A UAE residence address does not change the entry-visa position, which follows the passport. A temporary UAE passport does require a visa; a normal one does not.

tiers.name: New Zealand citizen
tiers.summary: No student visa. A New Zealand citizen can study on a Special Category visa granted on arrival, though fees are charged at the international rate unless residency tests are met.

tiers.name: All other non-citizens
tiers.summary: A subclass 500 student visa, with the Genuine Student requirement, OSHC for the whole visa period, and the AUD 2,500 application charge.

notes.cbse: A recognised qualification at every Go8 university, but each one converts it on a different scale - percentages, best-four aggregates, 20-point scales. A single 'Indian cutoff' is wrong nearly everywhere.
notes.isc: Recognised on the same basis; conversion differs by university exactly as it does for CBSE.
notes.state: Recognised, but several universities apply a lower conversion to state boards than to CBSE and ISC.
notes.ib: Converted through a published IB-to-ATAR table, which makes it the most predictable route for entry scores.
notes.alevel: Converted through a published A-Level-to-ATAR table; the best three or four subjects are counted depending on the university.
notes.us: Usually needs SAT or AP alongside the diploma to generate a comparable rank.

options.name: India
options.note: India sits in a higher evidence tier at most providers, which means the financial-capacity and Genuine Student evidence is read more strictly than the published minimum suggests.

options.name: UAE
options.note: Evidence level is set by the passport and the provider together, not by the UAE address. An Indian passport holder in Dubai is generally assessed on the Indian evidence level.

_meta.note: Each axis is keyed on what the official source keys on. APS follows the board, Etudes en France follows residence, the MVV follows the passport.
